title: When the user has denied notification permission, each refresh tick while a window stays above a threshold makes one failed add() and writes one error-level log line, because unmark re-arms the crossing every time.
evidence: The in-code comment at line 133 documents this trade-off. At the default 300 s cadence it adds up to about 12 log lines per hour per window. A later fix could check authorizationStatus == .denied (cached) and skip unmark or downgrade the log level. This is outside the scope of the fix.

title: The report's files list names Tests/AiTaskbarCoreTests/DiskCacheTests.swift, but git status shows no change to that file in the working tree.
evidence: The third item in CQ-MAE-012 (the DiskCacheTests name still saying payload_age) was not touched in this diff. DiskCacheTests.swift:99 payload_age_uses_injected_clock is still accurate, because it exercises freshPayloadWithAge, which is built on the private payloadAge() (DiskCache.swift:89). No defect, only a report inaccuracy.

Hidden cost introduced by the CQ-MAE-012 fix (NotificationService.swift:127-138): while notification authorization stays denied, every refresh tick with a window at or above its threshold makes one failed add() and writes one AppLog.lifecycle.error line. That is about 1 per 300 s per affected window, indefinitely, and the user sees nothing. It is cheap, but it is unbounded log noise. Consider a performance-lens follow-up: stop re-arming after a notificationsNotAllowed failure once authorization is known to be .denied, or rate-limit the log line.

The CQ-MAE-011 trade-off (Settings UI has no controls for gemini.prefer_antigravity, xai.prefer_grok_cli, xai.grok_base_url) is recorded only in B16-final-r2.report.json notes. When the ledger is updated, record it on the finding as a partial/accepted trade-off with a reopen_if (for example, if users report editing config.toml for these keys), so the finding does not read as fully closed.

NotificationService.swift:203-207: on a failed add(), unmark drops the key instead of restoring the previously delivered lower mark. If the next reading falls to a lower threshold that was already delivered, the user gets a duplicate notification, for example 70 delivered, 90 failed, next reading 75 re-sends 70. Low severity. A possible fix is to keep the prior mark and restore it.
